27.content:
# claude.md - Federation of State Boards of Physical Therapy (tree 293908919)

## Purpose
FSBPT (BPOA suborg, org 605410) agent call-handling guide: caller verification, password/email resets, ATT letter and exam status, FAQ library (persistent buttons: FAQs 41, Transfer to Survey 5, Licensing Board Numbers 50), and an AI website search.

## Architecture
Only the website-search lane is mapped here; the FAQ and verification screens are static content.
- 41 SearchPage -> 106 Ask caller's question for website search (hidden Website = fsbpt.org, ptcompact.org; text question)
- 106 -> 107 Search FSBPT websites with OpenAI (Data, Connected Object 800 alias webscraper)
- 107 -> 3 Strip scripts from website answer (Script) -> 108 Show website answer
- 108 buttons: Search Again -> 106, Not Able to Assist -> 6

## Data dictionary
- Website (form, node 106 hidden field) -> read by CO 800 payload ${Website}
- question (form, node 106) -> read by CO 800 payload ${question}
- actions.webscraper (CO 800, OpenAI chat completions) -> choices[0].message.content, _zt_meta.response.code; read only by node 3
- transforms.webscraper_answer_html (node 3) -> rendered by node 108

## External systems
- Connected Object 800 Webscraper, alias webscraper, POST https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions, gpt-4o. Prompt asks for an HTML fragment with an allowlist of display tags and no scripts, styles, forms or event handlers.

## Conventions & gotchas
- NEVER RENDER THE RAW OPENAI ANSWER. The model has returned a full HTML document with style, form and script blocks. Node 3 keeps only p, br, strong, em, b, i, u, ul, ol, li, h3, h4, table, thead, tbody, tr, th, td, a; drops every attribute except an https href on links; removes script/style/iframe/object/embed/form/svg/etc. with their contents. The prompt is a soft control; node 3 is the enforcement.
- escape_variable_output is 0 on this tree, so transforms render as HTML.

## Changelog
- 2026-10-05 - Brent / Claude - Engineering sanitization ticket (FSBPT case): added node 3 sanitizer between 107 and 108; 108 renders transforms.webscraper_answer_html instead of the raw answer; retitled 106-108; tightened CO 800 prompt; added this node - nodes 3, 27, 106, 107, 108

44.page_title: Caller needs assistance with reserving a seat for the exam/scheduling an appointment for the exam.
44.content: If the caller has received an Authorization to Test (ATT) letter, there are instructions on the letter to help schedule the appointment with Prometric. If the caller has not received an ATT letter because they are awaiting approval from the jurisdiction, please direct them to call the jurisdiction about the approval status. The jurisdiction contact number can be found here.

45.page_title: Caller needs assistance with refunds or with withdrawing from or re-registering for an exam.
45.content:
From the customer account, select “Withdraw from an Exam” under “Services”. The system will ask if the caller wants to completely withdraw or re-register for an exam. Follow the prompts from the system to withdraw. There are fees associated with withdrawing:

$50 if person is withdrawing more than 30 days before the exam date.

$120 if person withdrawing within 30 days of the exam date.

If re-registering, the fee is required before the re-registration can be processed.

46.page_title: Caller needs confirmation of payment for exam.
46.content: When someone registers for an exam, they receive a confirmation email. This email includes the amount the person paid for the exam.

47.page_title: Caller needs to know if the jurisdiction they transferred their score to has received the score.
47.content: When someone transfers their score to a jurisdiction, it is sent immediately; the jurisdiction has access to the score as soon as the request is submitted

48.page_title: Caller has a question about the type of identification accepted at Prometric testing centers
48.content:
Prometric requires one form of primary identification (unexpired, government-issued, photograph, pre-printed name and signature) and one form of secondary identification (unexpired, pre-printed name and signature). Prometric will accept two forms of primary ID.

Examples of primary IDs:

     Driver’s license

     Passport

     State-issued ID card


Examples of secondary IDs:

     Credit card

     ATM/Debit card

     School ID card

49.page_title: Caller has questions about the Authorization to Test (ATT) Letter.
49.content: This letter provides test takers with information on how to schedule the time and location of their exam. It includes instruction on how to schedule and details about the types of identification testing centers require. Candidates only receive this letter after being approved to take the exam. It can take up to 48 hours after approval for the letter to be emailed.

63.page_title: Caller has a question about the availability of the exam. Can it be taken any time of year?
63.content: The NPTE is offered four times a year for both exam levels (PT and PTA). It is offered in January, April, July and October.

64.page_title: Caller has a question about exceeding the number of attempts in a 12-month period.
64.content: The exam is only offered four times a year, in January, April, July, and October. If a test taker takes the exam on three consecutive administrations, they will need to skip an administration. For example, if someone takes the exam in April, July, and October of the same year, they will have to skip the January exam. The next time they will be able to test is April of the next year.

65.page_title: Caller did not complete their JAM exam before it expired.
65.content: There is a 96-hour window (four days) that the test taker must take the exam. If the exam is not completed in four days, they will need to repurchase the exam.

NOTE: The caller must select the correct (passing) score to send. If they accidentally send the incorrect score, they will need to be escalated.

79.page_title: Caller has question about when their free score report is available or how to access the free score report.
79.content: Free score reports are available approximately 10 business days after the exam. To view and download the free candidate score report, go to the Reports section of your Candidate Dashboard on the date listed in the table on the website https://www.fsbpt.org/Secondary-Pages/Exam-Candidates/National-Exam-NPTE/Dates-and-Deadlines. The free score report will remain viewable for thirty days. After thirty days reports may be purchased at the standard fee for an Individual Score Report.

81.page_title: If I move to the state where I hold my compact privilege, can that license be turned into a full state license?
81.content: No, your compact privilege cannot be used as a full state license.  You must submit a separate license application to the licensing state board.

82.page_title: What do I need to do if I change my permanent residence/home state?
82.content: If you have compact privileges and subsequently change your permanent residence/home state to a new state, you must report the change to the PT Compact Commission within 60 days. The best way to report the change is to login to your dashboard on ptcompact.org and change the address information. Note that changing a home state to a non-compact member state will terminate compact privileges. If changing from a home state to another compact member state, you must have a regular license in that state in order to maintain any current compact privileges.

83.page_title: How much does a Compact Privilege cost?
83.content: The fee to purchase Compact Privilege varies from state to state. There is a $45 Commission fee, and an optional state fee charged for each Compact Privilege. A list of state fees is available at https://ptcompact.org/process-and-requirements/.

84.page_title: How much does a Compact Privilege cost?
84.content: The fee to purchase Compact Privilege varies from state to state. There is a $45 Commission fee, and an optional state fee charged for each Compact Privilege. A list of state fees is available at https://ptcompact.org/process-and-requirements/.

85.page_title: Does a Compact Privilege allow the privilege holder to practice via telehealth in a remote state?
85.content: A Compact Privilege allows the privilege holder to practice physical therapy in a remote state under the scope of practice of the state where the patient/client is located, whether the practice is in-person or via telehealth. Compact privilege holders should consult the rules and laws for the state they wish to practice in to determine the specific telehealth requirements.

86.content: An adverse action is a publicly available disciplinary action taken against a license or compact privilege by a Licensing Board. Adverse action does not include non-disciplinary remediation required by the Licensing Board.

87.content: An encumbrance is any action taken by the Licensing Board that limits the practice or work of the physical therapist or physical therapist assistant. An encumbrance may be disciplinary or non-disciplinary in nature.

88.page_title: How and when do I self-report an encumbrance or adverse action?
88.content: A Compact Privilege holder must report to the Commission any encumbrance or adverse action placed upon any physical therapist or physical therapist assistant license held by the compact privilege holder in a non-member state within two (2) business days of the effective date of the action by sending an email to discipline@ptcompact.org.

89.page_title: Are fees waived for active-duty military, military spouses, or veterans?
89.content: Some member states have chosen to waive their state fees for active members of the military, spouses of active military, and former members of the military. Individuals who indicate they are active-duty military or veterans and provide required proof will have the state fees waived in the states where it is applicable. There is no waiver of the Commission fee. A list of member states waiving fees is available at https://ptcompact.org/process-and-requirements/

90.page_title: I moved, am I still eligible for Compact?
90.content: No. An individual cannot practice in a new home state with a compact privilege. Instead, the individual is responsible for applying for licensure by endorsement/reciprocity in the new state of residence. It is strongly recommended that this process is completed PRIOR to moving as obtaining a state-issued license can take several weeks.

91.page_title: I purchased a compact privilege for my home state, can I get a refund?
91.content: If you purchased a compact privilege for your home state, no refund will be issued after purchase.

92.page_title: My home state is not part of PT compact, but I have a license in a state that is.  Am I eligible for a compact privilege?
92.content: No, you need to hold a current, valid PT or PTA license in your home state of residence, which must be actively issuing and accepting compact privileges.

93.content: Compact privileges expiration date is tied to the expiration date of the home state license. Privileges will need to be repurchased after the home state license is renewed.

94.page_title: Can I renew my expired Compact License?
94.content: No, if your Compact License has expired you must repurchase the privilege the same way as last time.

95.page_title: Can I make a payment before the registration & payment deadline?
95.content: Yes, you can make a payment before the deadline date. You can go to the website https://www.fsbpt.org/Secondary-Pages/Exam-Candidates/National-Exam-NPTE/Dates-and-Deadlines and check the registration and payement deadlines.

96.page_title: Can I wait until payday to schedule my testing appointment?
96.content: Yes, you have up to the day before your eligibility window starts to schedule your testing appointment.

97.page_title: After I receive my ATT Letter will I be able to take the exam?
97.content: Yes, after you receive your ATT Letter, you will be eligible to take the exam.

98.page_title: Why does my dashboard say I'm ineligible?
98.content: If your NPTE registration status says ‘Eligibility (ineligible)’ it means you were not made eligible to sit for the exam by your licensing jurisdiction prior to the approval deadline. Since you were not made eligible prior to the deadline, we will issue a refund minus a $50 processing fee in the amount of $435 to the card that you used when making your original payment. Refunds will be processed in 5-10 business days.

99.page_title: I want to make a payment for the NPTE, but there is no pending payment.
99.content: For all fixed-date PT and PTA administrations there are strict deadlines for both registration, payment and jurisdiction approval. Go to Dates & Deadlines on the website https://www.fsbpt.org/Secondary-Pages/Exam-Candidates/National-Exam-NPTE/Dates-and-Deadlines for all applicable deadline information. Fixed date administrations are generally available for registration starting six months prior to the exam date. It is highly recommended that you register as early as possible.

100.page_title: Does the middle name on my ID matter?
100.content: No, the middle name on your ID does not matter. Only your first and last name on both forms of ID must exactly match the first and last name on your ATT letter issued by FSBPT.

101.page_title: Can I sit for the NPTE between the fixed dates listed on the website?
101.content: No, you cannot test between the fixed dates for PT and PTA administrations. The FSBPT only offers the NPTE 4 times a year for PT and PTA. Go to Dates & Deadlines on our website at https://www.fsbpt.org/Secondary-Pages/Exam-Candidates/National-Exam-NPTE/Dates-and-Deadlines and check the registration and payement deadlines.for all applicable deadline information. Fixed administration is available for registration approximately six months prior to the exam date. It is highly recommended that you register as early as possible.

102.page_title: Do I have to complete CEUs for my compact license?
102.content: No, CEUs are not required for a compact license.

103.page_title: What is the process to purchase a PT Compact license?
103.content:
To obtain a PT Compact privilege, you must first hold an active PT or PTA license in your home state, which must be a PT Compact member state. Then, you can verify your eligibility and purchase a Compact Privilege through the PT Compact website. This allows you to practice in other participating states without needing a separate license for each state. 

For a complete list of eligibility criteria and the step-by-step process please go to our website at https://ptcompact.org/process-and-requirements/

104.page_title: Calling about renewing their home state license
104.content: You will need to updated your home state license with the state before you can renew with us. Once you renew that license then you will be able to renew with us, but it will take about 1-2 business days for the process to complete.

105.content: The list of state boards and their contact information can be found here.

110.page_title: I want to transfer my score to another state but there is no eligible score to transfer.
110.content: If the system is unable to locate your score online, you must download the printable request form and follow the instructions at the bottom to securely upload completed form directly to FSBPT at www.fsbpt.org/scoredocs.

111.page_title: Do I need to submit my documents before I take the NPTE?
111.content:
This is a question for the PT state licensing board. 


The state board contact information can be found here. Find it and provide it to the caller if they need it.

112.page_title: I missed the deadline; can I still take the exam?
112.content: Unfortunately, the deadline to register for the exam has passed. There are no exceptions to the deadlines that have been set.

113.page_title: I want to update my AIN to my SSN.
113.content: If you receive an SSN in the future, please upload a copy of your Social Security card, both front and back, to: www.fsbpt.org/ainupdate. You must also notify the licensing authority from which you are seeking licensure of any updates to your name, or if you obtain an SSN.
